sovereign_country.strategic_role: 亚太高客单价数字内容、游戏出海与本土电商合规

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border E-Commerce Overseas Warehouse Order Fulfillment

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement Between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (signed 30 September 1992)
Convention Between the Republic of Korea and the Republic of Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income (signed 14 March 1979)
Free Trade Agreement Between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China (signed 1 June 2015)
Free Trade Agreement Between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (KORUS FTA, entered into force 15 March 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 543 et seq. (Yuhan Hoesa); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Act No. 12245, as amended, and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 18920, as amended (AML/CFT and UBO identification); Real Name Financial Transactions Act, Act No. 5493, as amended; Financial Services Commission regulations on customer identification and beneficial owner verification; Registration Tax Act and Education Tax Act as to registry fees.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the corporate founder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar or Companies Registry in the country of origin of the founder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing country is a Hague Apostille Convention member, obtain a single apostille from that country's designated competent authority; if the issuing country is not a member, obtain consular legalization from the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea with jurisdiction in that country. The apostille and consular legalization routes are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar or Companies Registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certificate if required by the issuing state, then either apostille (Hague member state) or consular legalize (non-member state) before submission to the Korean registry; do not apply both methods sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing Korean incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate founder, authenticated by the company secretary and notary public in the jurisdiction of the board
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized resolution or power of attorney must be apostilled by the competent authority in a Hague member state, or consular legalized by the Korean embassy/consulate in a non-member state. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, exclusive routes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of the corporate founder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar or founder, with a certified true copy issued by the registrar or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified articles are notarized and then apostilled if from a Hague Convention member; otherwise consular legalized by the Republic of Korea consular post in the issuing country. No sequential use of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the founder's principal banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate bank or correspondent bank having KYC/AML files for the founder and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The issuing bank must authenticate the signer's authority by notarization, and the notarized authority with the bank letter is then apostilled (Hague member state) or consular legalized (non-member state) as applicable; the two routes never converge.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, counterparties and freight or warehouse subcontractors must be screened before onboarding against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, Korean FIU/KOFIC designation lists, FSC financial restriction lists, the Korea Customs Trade Export Control System denial list, and domestic law-enforcement and insolvency watchlists. A risk-based assessment of domestic and foreign PEPs, their relatives and close associates, plus enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth verification, is mandatory. Any hit or adverse media triggers a written escalation to the AML compliance officer and, where required, a suspicious transaction report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit. All screening is refreshed within 24 hours before filing and every 30 days thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (iRO)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory identifier is the Hangul name; English or Latin script may appear only as a transliterated alias. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; (2) distinctive trade mark (sangho); (3) industry or business-purpose descriptor such as cross-dock or e-commerce fulfillment; and (4) optional English/Hanja transliteration. Hangul must follow the Revised Romanization guidelines, and the English name used on invoices, bank accounts and customs filings must match the registered Hangul name exactly for identity consistency.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name clearance may be renewed for one additional 30-day window by paying the search fee before expiration; if a conflicting registration intervenes, a fresh clearance must be filed. If the name is rejected, file a written objection with the competent local registry court, or with the Seoul Central District Court for centralized name cases, within 14 days of rejection; the objection must state the business scope and explain why the mark is distinguishable. If the registry court affirms the rejection, file an administrative appeal under the Commercial Registration Act and Administrative Litigation Act within 30 days. The rejected name cannot be used during appeal; a new name may be separately reserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not categorically illegal for company registration in South Korea, but the National Tax Service and commercial banks reject mailbox-only addresses for the ISIC 5210 cross-border e-commerce 3PL sector because VAT registration and settlement account onboarding require operational substance. A registered agent's address may be used temporarily for up to 90 days while the physical warehouse or logistics office lease is being completed. The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a physical place of business with lease evidence, local staff, warehouse equipment, inventory records and dispatch manifests; Korean banks, Airwallex and local ACH providers require a full lease agreement and utility bill before opening settlement accounts, and the business registration certificate will be issued only after the NTS verifies the place of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection readiness checklist: (1) executed lease for the registered address; (2) exterior signage matching the registered company name; (3) employment contracts and payroll records; (4) warehouse racking, equipment and goods; (5) dispatch, customs and inventory ERP logs; (6) VAT invoices and bank statements; (7) UBO and registry filings. Quant

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 287-2 through 287-74 (Limited Liability Company), together with the Commercial Registration Act and the Registration Tax Act
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division (Commercial Registration Section) of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office, supervised by the Supreme Court of Korea; online portal: Korean Commercial Registration Information System (IROS) at www.iros.go.kr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company filed with the District Court, accompanied by notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act; however, all subscribed cash capital must be fully paid into a branch of a Korean commercial bank before the incorporation registration, and the bank must issue a capital deposit certificate. The certificate is submitted to the Registry Court; there is no statutory post-registration blocked escrow. In-kind contributions must be appraised by a court-appointed or statutory appraiser, and title must be transferred to the Company prior to registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) EXECUTED IN WRITING ON [DATE] AT [CITY], REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The undersigned being all the initial directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), a Korean limited liability company organized under Articles 287-2 through 287-74 of the Korean Commercial Act, do hereby waive the formal meeting notice and consent to the following resolutions. WHEREAS the Company has been formed to conduct cross-border e-commerce order fulfillment, overseas warehouse operation, cross-dock logistics, bonded storage, and ancillary services; WHEREAS the founders have subscribed to all issued shares and have paid the subscription amount in full; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription and Issuance. The board ratifies and confirms the subscription of [NUMBER] common shares, each of par value [KRW AMOUNT], aggregating total share capital of [KRW AMOUNT]. The board declares that such capital has been fully paid by lawful cash deposits or in-kind contribution, and that the shares are validly issued, carefully confirming compliance with the Company's Articles and Korean law. 2. Banking Authorization. The board authorizes the Company to open corporate transaction, settlement, and payroll accounts at a reputable commercial bank in Seoul, and designates the Representative Director and the Operations Director as the sole authorized signatories, with a two-to-sign rule for any payment exceeding the Korean won equivalent of USD 20,000. The board instructs management to execute the bank's account signature cards and to maintain electronic banking credentials under dual control. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office and principal place of business in the Republic of Korea are fixed at [INSERT FULL KOREAN ADDRESS]. The directors are instructed to record this office as the statutory seat, to display the Company name at such location, and to file any subsequent change with the competent Registry Court without delay. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The board appoints [NAME] as Representative Director, [NAME] as Director of Operations, and [NAME] as Compliance Officer for logistics, customs, and data security affairs. The Representative Director is authorized to execute all incorporation follow-up documents, apply for warehouse and customs licenses, retain local counsel and accountants, and represent the Company before any governmental authority. 5. General Execution and Ratification. The board directs the officers to complete the commercial registry, business tax registration, warehouse operation registration, bonded warehouse license if applicable, environmental and fire safety clearances, and social insurance registrations. The board also resolves that any lawful act done prior to this resolution in the Company's name is hereby ratified. This resolution shall be effective immediately and remain in full force until revoked by a subsequent resolution.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal 'HomeTax' at www.hometax.go.kr; export customs declarations and UNI-PASS filings are administered by the Korea Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must obtain a Korean Business Registration Number (BRN) under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The entity must appoint a tax representative in Korea if it has no domestic place of business; register with the competent tax office via HomeTax within 20 days of commencing a taxable supply. Required documents include the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, branch registration certificate (if applicable), power of attorney for the tax representative, and non-resident identity/holding structure. The BRN is a 10-digit number that serves simultaneously as the VAT registration number, corporate income tax ID, and employer payroll account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax; no check-the-box or pass-through election is available for this entity type.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for corporate entities: every business operator must obtain a VAT registration (BRN) within 20 days of commencing business. For individual small merchants, simplified VAT filing applies when annual taxable revenue is below the statutory simplified-tax threshold (currently KRW 80 million).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-Tax Invoice issuance through the NTS HomeTax portal. Each VAT invoice must be issued electronically and transmitted to the NTS by the 20th day of the month following the taxable supply. There is no real-time pre-approval block; however, the NTS operates automated electronic invoice matching and risk-scoring. Businesses may also integrate ERP/accounting systems with HomeTax APIs for electronic submission. Fiscal anti-fraud digital stamping is not required for standard 3PL/export services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for 0% VAT once an Export Declaration is accepted by Korea Customs Service and the goods are actually removed from Korea. Services supplied to a non-resident recipient outside Korea (including cross-border logistic, warehousing, and delivery facilitation) are zero-rated under the Korean VAT Act as 'export services' when the recipient is located outside Korea and the service is wholly performed abroad or exported. The exporter must hold contractual evidence and payment in foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration Receipt issued electronically through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Commercial Invoice with overseas consignee and FOB/CIF value
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Airway Bill (AWB) evidencing cross-border carriage
Foreign Currency Acquisition Confirmation (Certificate of Receipt of Export Proceeds) issued by a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank, or bank remittance statement matching the invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that zero-rating was claimed without proof of actual export/repatriation or the transaction is fictitious, the 0% rate is retrospectively revoked; the taxpayer is assessed omitted VAT at 10%, plus additional tax penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Penalty rates escalate by violation type (up to 40% of the unpaid VAT), and criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act (including fines or imprisonment) may apply. The NTS also has authority to cancel the initial tax refund and impose statutory interest from the date of repayment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Foreign Exchange Administration of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), acting through licensed foreign exchange banks in South Korea.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a managed float and the Korean won is freely convertible for current account payments and receipts such as cross-border logistics fees, cargo transportation charges, and warehousing revenue. Capital transactions are not unrestricted: an inbound equity investment, a loan, or a profit distribution above the current account framework must go through a licensed foreign exchange bank and be filed on the Foreign Exchange Information System under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. There is no foreign currency surrender requirement for export sales, and the entity may maintain foreign exchange deposit accounts in the bank where the export receipt is collected. Dividend and branch remittances by a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa are permitted after domestic tax clearance, audited financial statements, and a shareholder resolution, but the bank must receive a payment purpose code and supporting documents. In practice, the main operational restriction is documentary rather than quantitative: each outward remittance must be accompanied by a real underlying trade invoice or service contract. The MOEF/BOK retains emergency stabilization powers, but ordinary current account transactions remain settled on a same-day or T+1 basis through bank-owned clearing rails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must generally be collected within six months from the export declaration date unless the Korean foreign exchange bank approves an extension based on the goods movement, letter-of-credit tenor, or supplier payment terms. The collection is reported through the bank to the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Information System and to the Korea Customs Service to close the underlying export declaration. No fixed percentage of export foreign currency receipts must be converted to KRW. The exporter may retain 100 percent of such proceeds in a domestic foreign currency deposit account or convert them to Korean won at the prevailing market rate; only the reporting of receipt and legal custody of the foreign exchange within a licensed bank is mandatory.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow and KRW Basic Operating Account
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and KRW Settlement Account
Capital Verification Account under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Trade Dedicated SWIFT Account
Basic Operational Currency Account plus Treasury Hedging Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as the sole treasury rail. While Airwallex and global EMIs are accepted as a supplementary settlement engine for collection from overseas marketplaces and are useful for non-KRW multi-currency balances, a foreign EMI without a Korean Electronic Financial Business Registration cannot hold KRW current accounts on behalf of a Korean legal entity. The Korean entity must clear inbound share capital, export surrender reporting, and KRW liquidity through a licensed Tier-1 bank; the EMI channel is legally acceptable only for ancillary FX conversion and offshore pooling when routed through partner banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks require physical attendance at the branch for initial onboarding of the legal entity and at least one statutory director. A remote consular proxy opening is not acceptable for a non-resident-owned Korean LLC because the bank must verify the real person, the title to sign, and the source of funds under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act. The practical path is an in-branch interview by the authorized Korean-resident director or a locally appointed authorized officer holding an original notarized, apostilled Power of Attorney from the UBO. For the foreign investment capital escrow account, the foreign investor should also appear in person or use a Korean counsel with a specific Power of Attorney, and all passport and registration documents must be Korean-translated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner of the non-resident parent or cross-border investor is absent and appears only through a proxy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A completed UBO declaration on the bank's prescribed form; notarized certificate of incorporation and current shareholder register of the investing entity; passport-quality copies of all shareholders holding 10 percent or more; an apostilled corporate resolution; a notarized Korean translation of every document; and an organizational chart evidencing no nominee holdings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company's declared business is ISIC 5210 warehousing and cross-docking, but the payment pattern shows high volumes of B2C e-commerce flowing to overseas 3PL warehouses with no invoice or cargo trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of order-level export logs, shipping carrier waybills, customs export declarations from the Korean electronic trade settlement system, warehouse management system stock records, signed fulfilment agreements from each marketplace or customer, and service invoices priced on a clear per-order or per-pallet basis; an auditor's reconciliation of payment amounts to manifests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound share capital injection originates from mixed-source funds or a jurisdiction with no evident business nexus to the Korean logistics entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve to twenty-four months of bank statements from the investor's licensed financial institution, source-of-funds documentation including tax returns, audited financials and sale or purchase agreements, the approved foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the bank's deposit certificate for investment money, and a business plan or capex budget showing use of the capital for warehouse deposits, lease guarantees, equipment, and initial operating cash.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected trade-based money laundering through inflated 3PL service fees charged by related overseas warehouse entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An independent transfer pricing documentation package for intra-group logistics services; a benchmark or comparability study showing arm's-length per-order warehouse fees; the full master warehouse service agreement; reconciliation from the foreign customer's purchase orders to warehouse dispatch records; and a CPA's comfort letter on fee calculations, supported by electronic freight audit and payment records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident investors should first file a foreign investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or Invest KOREA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, then remit investment cash through the designated Korean Tier-1 bank using SWIFT MT103 with the FEIS purpose code covering foreign direct investment by share subscription. The remittance must name the Yuhan Hoesa as beneficiary, include the foreign investment report number if available, and identify the investing entity. The receiving bank should be instructed to credit a foreign-invested company capital deposit or escrow account and to issue a foreign investment capital deposit certificate; the company's auditor uses this bank certificate to complete capital verification for registration with the Korean court registry and tax office. After payment, the foreign investor must file the foreign investment report and obtain the Foreign Enterprise Registration Certificate within the statutory window. Fund release follows share issuance and is recorded on the Foreign Exchange Information System; all valuations should use the bank's telegraphed transfer rate or finance market average rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border payments of overseas 3PL service fees and inventory purchases; for larger purchase orders use irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit issued through a Tier-1 Korean bank; for stable recurring supplier payments use Documentary Collections in D/P or D/A form. For domestic KRW treasury movements, use the KFTC ACH and BOK-Wire+; for customs-related export declarations and logistics evidence, use the electronic trade settlement system to reconcile physical cargo movement with the FX payment. All outbound payments must be supported by an underlying contract, invoice, tax invoice, and if goods are moved from Korea, the export customs declaration and bill of lading or airway bill. The bank will apply the appropriate FEIS purpose code and may require annual transfer pricing documentation if a portion of the fee is paid to a related offshore warehouse entity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Permissible FX forwards: onshore KRW/USD forward contracts limited to settlement of confirmed receivables or payables under service and trade contracts, with tenor aligned to invoice maturity and bank-approved counterparty limits.

Permissible NDFs: non-deliverable forwards are only available where the Korean won cannot be physically delivered, must be based on a real commercial exposure, and require submission of underlying trade documents plus a bank-compliance statement.

Permissible currency swaps: executed only for the purpose of matching a cross-border loan, capital injection, or dividend hedging program, not for speculative positions, and must be approved by the foreign exchange bank with a clear FX exposure report and threshold limit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return with statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax; local corporate income tax component remitted to the competent local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; by 31 March for calendar-year companies; an extension of up to 1 month may be available only by formal NTS approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional 40% penalty on unpaid corporate tax; underreporting triggers 20%; overdue tax bears daily interest of 0.022% per day; persistent delinquency can result in NTS enforced collection, business licence suspension, and criminal fines but does not immediately trigger a corporate strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Change Filings and Statutory Register Updating (members, directors, auditors, registered office, charges/mortgages)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local District Court Commercial Registration Office under the Supreme Court of South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks of any change in registered directors, statutory representatives, registered members, registered office, or registered charges; no annual renewal form is required for unchanged companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing registrations are punishable by fines up to KRW 5 million (approximately USD 3,800) under the Korean Commercial Act; continued non-compliance may produce conflicting public records and court-initiated corrective orders; administrative strike-off is not the standard remedy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Foreign-Invested Enterprise Status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For foreign-invested enterprises, the annual status report covering the preceding fiscal year must be submitted by 31 March of the following year; every reportable shareholding transfer must additionally be filed within 30 days of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign-investment status report can result in administrative fines up to approximately KRW 2 million, loss of foreign-investment registration status, and forfeiture of available foreign-investment tax incentives

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Auditor Appointment and Audited Financial Statements Delivery (where statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service in conjunction with the Financial Supervisory Service electronic filing system (where applicable); audited statements are also submitted to the annual general meeting of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: External auditor appointment must be made by the annual members' meeting before the audit period; audited financial statements must be completed and presented to members within 3 months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company required to undergo external audit that fails to appoint an auditor or obtain an audit report is subject to administrative fines and criminal sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Companies; the tax authorities may additionally reject the corporate tax return as incomplete and levy a 20% assessment correction penalty

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Companies, a Korean Yuhan Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit if total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million). Additional mandatory audit triggers apply to listed companies, companies preparing for listing, financial institutions, and companies whose industry or parent-company status is expressly designated by the Financial Services Commission. Headcount is not a stand-alone statutory audit trigger in Korea; the decisive quantitative tests are asset-based. A company below the asset threshold is legally exempt from mandatory external audit, but lenders, contractual covenants, or the court may still request an agreed-upon or independent review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed companies and specifically designated financial or large private companies; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) apply to other private companies; micro and small non-public Yuhan Hoesa entities may apply the Sunshine Accounting Standards / SME Accounting Standards where permitted by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not currently require a standalone annual UBO certificate filing for an ordinary private Yuhan Hoesa. The company must nevertheless maintain a current and accurate member register. If the Yuhan Hoesa is a foreign-invested enterprise, any transfer of membership quotas, change of a foreign investor, or capital change must be reported to KOTRA/MOTIE within 30 days of the event, and an annual foreign-investment status report must be filed by 31 March. Domestic share transfers must be recorded in the member register and reported to the commercial registration office within 2 weeks. Corporate secretarial practice must also require AML/KYC files to identify natural persons who ultimately hold or control the company.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive rates under Article 55 of the Korean Corporate Tax Act: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; and 24% above KRW 300 billion (headline top statutory rate 24%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises in Korean Free Economic Zones may obtain a 50% corporate tax reduction for 3 years and 30% for the subsequent 2 years; R&D tax credits up to 30-50% are available, and certain green logistics or warehouse automation investments under the Tax Incentives Limitation Law may qualify for accelerated depreciation; the patent box regime is not generally available in Korea, but royalty income from registered Korean patents may benefit from reduced IP income weighting in the CJEU?

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Tax Base and Tax Computation Return) filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax system; the standard schedule for Korean entities is identified in the Korean Corporate Tax Return package, with Form 32-60 used for the local income tax surcharge computation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a semi-annual preliminary corporate tax return is separately required for fiscal years longer than six months, payable within two months after the end of the preliminary tax period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Corporate Tax Return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year-end), and the tax must be paid by the same deadline unless an NTS-approved extension or a tax treaty timeline modifies the due date; extensions are generally limited and require material justification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification, head office location, and effective place of management (POEM) declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether this Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation with worldwide income or a foreign corporation with Korean-sourced income. If the POEM is outside Korea, only income attributable to a Korean permanent establishment (PE) is taxable, and the return must attach a PE income-allocation schedule; non-resident shareholders must provide their residency jurisdiction to enable treaty analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts and revenue from cross-dock fulfillment and overseas e-commerce warehousing services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report storage fees, picking and packing fees, last-mile delivery management fees, and customer service handling fees actually derived from the Korean warehouse. Do not include customs duties or freight charges collected on behalf of cargo owners; the entire fulfillment revenue may be treated as Korean-source from a business PE if the contract identifies the Korean warehouse as the fulfillment performance location.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses, intercompany charges, and cost-sharing rearrangements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct ordinary and necessary logistics operating expenses, but add back non-deductible corporate income tax, penalties, political donations, and related-party fees that lack business substance. For management fees, software royalties, and foreign subcontractor costs, apply the OECD arm’s length Standard and be prepared to substantiate that the Korean entity actually bore the cost and alone enjoyed the benefit; transfer-pricing adjustments must be reflected in the tax schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and set-off of carried-forward tax losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax losses incurred by the Korean branch may be carried forward for 10 years, but only against the same business or income category if the foreign corporation confines its Korean activity through a PE. Attach a complete loss carry-forward schedule and reconcile book and tax income; a foreign corporation that loses its Korean PE may pre-emptively lose the right to future loss offsets and must report that timing issue in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional non-resident branch tax or retributive tax on unreinvested earnings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the entity is owned by a foreign shareholder or is a branch of a foreign corporation, compute the branch profits tax under Article 96(2) of the Corporate Tax Act at 20% of unreinvested taxable income after corporate income tax, unless a bilateral treaty lowers or eliminates that branch tax. Attach evidence of reinvestment, board resolutions, and treaty residency certificates; failure to do so will result in deemed distribution at the statutory 22% effective rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax amount and local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the national corporate tax at the progressive rates, then add 10% local income tax (surtax) on the national tax payable. Non-resident investors must separately identify any foreign tax credits, treaty credits, and withholding taxes already paid on intercompany dividends or royalties; the NTS will require a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration to grant unilateral or treaty foreign tax relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Negligent failure to file triggers a 20% penalty on the unpaid tax; false or fraudulent filing triggers a 40% penalty; unpaid tax is subject to daily late-payment surcharges (approximately 0.022% per day, which the NTS adjusts periodically to the statutory annual rate); criminal fraud thresholds apply when a taxpayer intentionally files a false return with the intent to evade, carrying liability under the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act of imprisonment for up to 3 years or fines up to 3 times the evaded tax, plus director blacklisting and forced collection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding under Article 156(1) of the Corporate Tax Act, plus 2% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, producing a 22% effective statutory rate on outbound cash dividends to non-resident shareholders not entitled to treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral Double Tax Agreement (DTA) relief, the non-resident shareholder or branch must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign country’s competent authority, (ii) submit the TRC to the Korean withholding agent before payment, together with a formal beneficial ownership declaration naming the ultimate owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty, and (iii) file the prescribed treaty-claim form on the NTS HomeTax portal, including evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period to support the 5% or 15% treaty rate for dividends. The Korean withholding agent must retain the TRC and declaration in its payroll or tax file; refund applications may be filed within 3 years after the end of the withholding month if the reduced treaty rate is not applied in time.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding tax on cross-border royalties and interest is 20% national tax plus a 2% local tax surcharge, aggregating to 22% on gross payments. Bilateral treaties commonly reduce interest withholding to 5%-15% and royalty withholding to 5%-10% depending on the country and specific tax treaty articles, but the reduced rate is only effective after the withholding agent receives the TRC and beneficial ownership evidence; intercompany lending from a non-resident affiliate must satisfy the Korean thin-capitalization and anti-round-tripping rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance_.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Article 11 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LCITA), the local file and master file must be prepared and submitted when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion during the fiscal year; a country-by-country report is required when the consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 700 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance_.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean tax authorities apply the substance-over-form principle and the OECD BEPS anti-abuse rules; a logistics company with no actual warehouse employees, no inventory control, no local managerial risk-bearing, and no core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea may be disregarded or recharacterized, causing the denial of treaty benefits, re-attribution of operating income to the foreign parent, and potential assessment of the 22% branch withholding tax on fictitious income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of cross-dock service revenue, fabrication of warehouse rent or subcontracted logistics expenses, or engaging in a circular intercompany royalty scheme whose dominant purpose is to obtain a tax benefit without a substantive commercial reason.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 40% of the underreported tax (20% where the failure to file is negligent) under Article 47-2 through 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily late-payment surcharges and, if fraudulent, criminal fine under the Punishment for Tax Evasion Act of up to 3 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subjected to joint and several liability for the corporate tax under Article 42 of the Commercial Act and civil asset restitution to the NTS; willful evasion triggers imprisonment for up to 3 years, travel blacklisting through the NTS international tax cooperation procedure, and freezing of personal bank accounts, with no suspension of the limitation period until the tax is paid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare, disclose, or submit the master file, local file, or country-by-country report when intercompany transactions exceed the KRW 10 billion threshold, or knowingly applying non-arm’s length pricing using unsupported allocation ratios for warehouse profit, storage rents, and logistics software services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory tax adjustment using the best arm’s length method and an added penalty of 10%-20% of the understated tax under Article 12 of the LCITA, in addition to a fine up to KRW 100 million for non-submission of the required documents; in egregious cases the NTS may apply a broader anti-avoidance recharacterization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors owe a statutory duty to complete and sign the transfer pricing documentation; failure can make them personally liable for penalties and accrued interest, and they may be exposed to criminal sanctions if they certified false information; NTS may issue a forced collection attachment against director personal assets and impose international travel bans pending resolution of the adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell or Economic Substance Abuse and Tax Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Yuhan Hoesa as a pass-through shell with no physical warehouse, no local employees, no local management personnel, and no logistics inventory in Korea, while flows of e-commerce settlement funds pass through the entity solely to access a lower dividend or royalty tax treaty and avoid the real economic burden of the Korean logistics operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefits under anti-abuse provisions and possible unilateral recharacterization of all Korean-source income as taxable PE income of a foreign parent; civil penalties for failure to maintain meaningful substance may include cancellation of corporate identity under court orders and AML/CFT reporting fines for unexplained clearing transactions of up to KRW 500 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts may pierce the corporate veil when the company is a sham or may be equated with the foreign parent’s alter ego, making directors jointly liable for all underpaid enterprise-scale taxes; criminal exposure reaches imprisonment for up to 10 years under Article 355 of the Criminal Act for breach of duty or embezzlement where logistics business assets were diverted, and directors may be blacklisted from leaving Korea and have their passports suspended.
